notes.title: Interim Patch
notes.content:
[p][/p][p]Interim Patch (Pre-Patch 1)[/p][p]We’ve released an interim patch in our lead-up to Patch 1. A larger first patch will be released for all platforms as soon as possible, but in the meantime please continue to report any bugs to our support team at [/p][p][url="https://support.aspyr.com"]support.aspyr.com[/url][/p][p][/p][p]
[/p][p][b]Full Changelist:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue that could occur when joining a Persistent World server where the cursor was missing and controllers would not function on the loading screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a crash that could occur when using custom emotes from modules or Persistent Worlds.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Quicksave not being able to be re-bound in the Keymapping Tab [b](Steam only)[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the default keybind for Quicksave was also the default shortcut for “Take Screenshot” [b](Steam only)[/b][/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fixed a crash that could occur when using the Staff of the Magi.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some UI mods displayed unintended blue artifacts.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue when connecting to Persistent World servers where the Progress Bar displayed misleading information.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue on Persistent World servers where Server Vault character names and information would not display correctly in the Select Character list.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Local Vault characters would appear in the Select Character list on servers that had the “Local Character Allowed” option turned off.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue on Persistent World servers where texture maps could flicker when clipping the camera through certain assets in large areas.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Neverwinter Nights 2: Enhanced Edition (PC) Review
notes.content:
Dungeons & Dragons and video games go together like peanut butter and jelly. So, given the premier tabletop game’s popularity in recent years, and the prevalence of 20-year-old games getting remastered, it’s no surprise that Neverwinter Nights 2: Enhanced Edition has rolled initiative and entered the scene.

Born from the popularity of D&D 3.5 and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, BioWare took their proven engine back to its d20-rolling roots with Neverwinter Nights, a sprawling campaign that gave players all the thrills of playing a game of D&D with higher production values and less math. Then, just as with Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords, development of Neverwinter Nights 2 fell to Obsidian Entertainment, who produced another admirable sequel.

And now, once again, the series is following KOTOR‘s trajectory, and has passed into the hands of Aspyr Media for a remaster.

notes.title: Neverwinter Nights 2 is one of the best RPGs you've never played, and if you like Baldur's Gate 3 or Disco Elysium, you owe it to yourself to check out its new Enhanced Edition
notes.content: I never want to be an RPG gatekeeper⁠—I want as many people as possible to find out what makes these games so great. But their inherent crustiness can make my old-head RPG favorites hard to recommend to people who haven't already bought in. I've got a lot of friends I recommend Disco Elysium to, but not very many I tell to play Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura... Read more.

notes.title: Neverwinter Nights 2: Enhanced Edition is an excellent, subtle remaster and my new Steam Deck game of the summer
notes.content: Neverwinter Nights 2 is one of my favorite games⁠—if you want to know why you should play it, I've got a separate write-up here. Even though NwN2 released in 2006 after the dawn of the Xbox 360, it's aged more poorly than many of its contemporaries and even predecessors, making it harder and harder to recommend over the years until now... Read more.
